newsitem.title: CANADA: TransCanada says natgas pipe was corroded.
newsitem.headline: TransCanada says natgas pipe was corroded.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd said on Thursday that it had yet to determine the cause of a natural gas pipeline break in Ontario, although some external corrosion on that part of the pipeline had been found.

TransCanada said investigators from Canada's Transportation Safety Board and National Energy Board were expected to arrive later Thursday to begin examinations into the incident, which occurred late Wednesday.
"Without prejudging the results of the investigations, we observed some external corrosion on that section of pipe," TransCanada vice-president John Walker said in a statement.
"What role it played in the rupture will be determined by the investigations."
Late on Wednesday, a section of pipeline ruptured on the company's mainline near Vermilion Bay in northwestern Ontario.
Escaping gas caught fire and burned itself out after the break was isolated by closing valves on either side of it, the company said.
TransCanada said its personnel were on the scene to assist investigators, conduct the company's own investigation and mobilize repair crews when the site was released to the company.
The affected section of pipe was to remain isolated until investigations and repairs were completed.

The company, which operates the 6.7 billion cubic feet a day cross-Canada mainline, said natural gas was being routed around the site through adjacent pipelines and that firm deliveries were not not affected.
Traffic on the nearby Trans Canada Highway, the country's main east-west roadway, was disrupted by the incident.
